Key Research Thinking Patterns: Quantum Confinement Bandgap Engineering: Utilizing strain-balanced multi-quantum well structures in IV-VI semiconductors to precisely tune absorption spectra and optimize current matching in multi-junction devices (e.g., PbSnSe/PbSrSe MQWs with 1.4-3.5 nm well widths).

Spectroscopic Trace Gas Detection: Employing mid-infrared Interband Cascade Lasers coupled with Herriott multipass cells and second-harmonic detection to identify low-concentration metabolic biomarkers in complex headspace environments (e.g., acetaldehyde sensing for cancer metabolism).

Thermodynamic-Economic System Integration: Coupling high-temperature thermal radiator physics with Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) modeling to validate the commercial viability of thermal energy grid storage systems against conventional battery technologies.

Analytical Device Physics Optimization: Deriving closed-form expressions for intrinsic carrier density, reverse bias saturation current, and internal quantum efficiency to predict and enhance open-circuit voltage and fill factor in narrow-bandgap photovoltaic architectures.
Summary Description: Patrick J. McCann bridges high-efficiency thermophotovoltaic (TPV) energy systems and advanced biomedical sensing. In energy, he engineers IV-VI semiconductor MQW devices (PbSnSe/PbSrSe) using strain and quantum confinement to optimize TPV conversion for molten silicon storage, integrating LCOE modeling for grid-scale decarbonization. In biomedicine, he applies mid-IR Interband Cascade Laser (ICL) absorption spectroscopy to detect trace metabolic biomarkers like acetaldehyde in cell culture headspace. By leveraging second-harmonic detection and multipass gas cells, he enables real-time monitoring of HIF-1α-driven cancer metabolism shifts. This dual trajectory highlights his expertise in semiconductor physics, ranging from bulk device optimization to precision molecular spectroscopy for diagnostic applications.
